title: Check compensated BIT shear cuts and a complete q-gauge control
body:
The two compensated shear cuts have minima 4 and 5, or 60 and 5 with anchored inputs. A literal macro-level q compensation preserves all 38-root outputs both ways but adds 777 paid grade-one positions.

## Scope and source

Retains the original native calls and applies the positive monomial stage rule in the declared shear model. Physical inverse-bearing or nonlocal gates remain open. The complete source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit-compensated-shear-cut/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 -I -B check.py` passed the independent cuts, both complete formal caller orientations and the directed full invoice. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

A cheaper gauge requires a different grammar or a physically realized inverse gate and complete price and tape replay.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
